target_customer: Fast-growing startups and mid-size tech companies moving off QuickBooks, Xero or NetSuite
problem: Startups outgrow QuickBooks but find NetSuite and other legacy ERPs slow and costly, so month-end close and reporting stay manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for accounting and ERP, plus implementation and migration services

founders.name: John Glasgow
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; Invoice2go was acquired by Bill.com, with the price shown as 625M or 600M+ on the page.

founders.name: Fernando
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only a first name; credited with scaling Invoice2go and Trovata alongside John.

technical_complexity.rationale: A multi-entity general ledger, revenue recognition and close tooling is demanding accounting software, but built on standard engineering; the AI features came later.

defensibility.rationale: ERP and ledger data are deeply embedded once migrated, though AI-native rivals such as Rillet and DualEntry copy the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were described as legacy and slow to respond; newer AI-native rivals (Rillet, DualEntry) emerged and raised large rounds by 2025. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. Later case studies and a tracker estimate of 20 to 30 percent of customers migrating from NetSuite point to demand from startups outgrowing QuickBooks.

branding.domain_note: Uses campfire.ai; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Modern finance, with an assistant called Ember AI

branding.brand_signature: Campfire and Ember AI naming theme
branding.community_and_virality: Some press describes it as Slack for accounting; no other community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly real-word name and a consistent fire theme, strong trade press, but the name is shared with many unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Campfire entered YC in Summer 2023 with a founder who came from Invoice2go and Bill.com, and sold a modern general ledger to startups leaving QuickBooks and NetSuite. It raised a $35M Series A led by Accel in June 2025 and a $65M Series B about 12 weeks later, reportedly 100M+ in total, with named fast-growing customers and case studies. Self-reported growth and a crowded AI-native ERP field are the main caveats.
notes: Series B valuation of 375M is a tracker estimate. Total raised reported as 103.5M, which implies about 3.5M of earlier funding not identified, so an earlier seed is missing from rounds. Competitor search returned only 2024 and later entrants, so list is empty. Founder Fernando surname and both founders education not found. Series A investor list from a press release summary.
